releaseRecommendation: All 27 previously reported factual and clinical-safety blockers remain resolved, with no remaining true blockers. RTP generated suffixes and malformed stems are gone. targetedVerification.text: Which source should be investigated more carefully?
options: The lumbar spine and neural pathways
The adductor alone because any tenderness is diagnostic
targetedVerification.correctOption: The lumbar spine and neural pathways
targetedVerification.passage: A 29-year-old footballer presents with groin pain, reduced lumbar movement and intermittent numbness into the posterior thigh. Adductor palpation is mildly uncomfortable but does not reproduce the athlete's main pain.
targetedVerification.explanation: Lumbar movement restriction and distal sensory symptoms make a spinal or neural contribution important to assess.
targetedVerification.finding: The corrected keyed option is grammatically complete and clinically supported by the passage. The reduced lumbar movement and posterior-thigh numbness justify investigating lumbar/neural contribution; mild adductor discomfort without reproduction of the main pain does not make the adductor-only distractor correct.

methodology.blockerRule: A true blocker requires an incorrect or materially ambiguous key, a passage that does not support the keyed decision, unsafe clinical management for the stated facts, or a keyed option too incomplete to answer unambiguously. Minor grammar, a dangling punctuation mark with an otherwise clear answer, repeated templates, broad locators, and length bias are non-blocking flags.

verificationSummary.lower: All progression and bone-stress escalation keys now select case-relevant pain recurrence, persistent deficit, focal rest/night pain, or reduced walking load tolerance. The mixed Doha item now asks for the specific resisted-hip-flexion finding.
verificationSummary.spine: All previously incomplete keyed options are complete and clinically interpretable. Pars loading, dose tolerance, pelvic/adductor rehabilitation, MRI correlation, Doha findings, load monitoring, and hip-motion effects remain supported.
verificationSummary.emergency: The day-four concussion case now advances symptom-limited non-contact work; the mild/brief symptom-rise case holds and reassesses; the two unsupported Doha coexistence cases select the supported pubic-related presentation.
verificationSummary.heat: The oriented, improving heat-illness case now uses active cooling, monitoring, supervised observation, and escalation for worsening mental status/symptoms rather than an automatic heat-stroke transport key.

contentReview.finding: The new concise keyed spine options preserve the relevant clinical proposition in the sampled and targeted items. Examples include pars loading, neurological red flags, dose tolerance, MRI clinical correlation, Doha examination, neural contribution, and load monitoring.

SCAT6Amsterdam.finding: Removal for suspected concussion/red flags, Child SCAT6 age use, relative rest, symptom-limited activity, at-least-24-hour RTS spacing, return-to-learn sequencing, and mild/brief symptom handling remain aligned with the local Amsterdam consensus PDF.

DohaGroin.finding: The repaired iliopsoas, pubic-related, coexisting-entity, MRI-correlation, and adductor-examination items remain supported by the local Doha consensus PDF.

heatIllnessAndSpinalTrauma.finding: The targeted heat-illness and spinal-trauma keys remain clinically safe for their stated passages. Residual concerns are template repetition and option length only.

malformedPunctuationAndEllipsis.finding: No ellipsis, repeated punctuation, space-before-punctuation, leading punctuation, dangling punctuation, or duplicate-word corruption was found across the current bank.

optionLengthBias.metric: Strictly longest/shortest correct options, correct option at least 10 characters above the three-distractor median, and option spread above 15/20 characters.
optionLengthBias.finding: The global strictly-longest rate is 34.9%, just below the 35% review target. The latest spine pass removed padding but shortened many distractors as well, leaving 79/200 spine correct options strictly longest and 73/200 at least 10 characters above the three-distractor median. Upper extremity remains 135/200 strictly longest. This is a significant answer-detection risk, but not a factual blocker when the options remain clinically plausible.

sourceLocatorQuality.finding: Every question has one resolving primary sourceId. Some textbook entries remain broad book-level locators rather than exact chapter/page citations.
